title: Scheduled
empty: There are no scheduled tasks. A task runs on its own, with DBine closed: a script, an export, a schema comparison or a backup.
saveFirst: Save your changes before running it
deleteConfirm: Delete the task “{{name}}”? It stops running and its history is erased.
notScheduled: The task was saved, but the system didn't schedule it: {{error}}
approvalChanged: What the task changes is no longer what you approved (a file changed in the meantime): review it again.
prodHint: Changes data on a production connection

when.title: When
when.hint: Runs with DBine closed, as long as your user is signed in. If the computer was off, it runs when it's turned back on.

notify.title: Notify
notify.failure: If it fails or finds differences

varsHint: In file names, scripts, emails and messages you can use:
varsHintText: Only in the text of emails and messages:

onError.stop: If it fails, stop the task
onError.continue: If it fails, continue with the next one

step.continueOnError: Continue with the next statement if one fails
step.header: Column names in the first row
step.compareHint: If the databases differ, it saves the script that takes the database to compare to the reference one and sends a notification. The script is not run.
step.noNative: This engine has no backups of its own: the task makes a DBine copy (structure and data in a script).

mail.subject: Subject
mail.htmlBodyHint: Optional: an HTML file used as the email body (the text is kept for clients that don't show HTML). {steps.1.html} is the HTML export of a "Run notebook" step.
mail.attachmentsHint: File paths, with variables: {steps.1.file} is the file from step 1. If an attachment doesn't exist, the step fails. Attachments can add up to 20 MB.

whenOptions.alert: A previous step raised an alert

mail.errorsHint: For the email to go out when a step fails, that step must be set to "If it fails, continue with the next one".
mail.noServer: The mail server is not configured yet.

approve.title: This task changes data or structure
approve.text: These steps will run on their own, with nobody reviewing them first. Check which database they point to:
approve.production: There are steps on production connections.

notebook.hint: Runs all cells in order, like "Run all", and stops at the first one that fails. It asks nothing: whatever asks for confirmation in the app has to be allowed here.
notebook.noCells: The notebook has no SQL cells.
notebook.writes: Changes data ({{what}}): approved when the task is saved.
notebook.confirmHint: In the app, these databases ask for confirmation before running (confirmation environment or production connection). A task can't confirm: without the permission, the cell fails.
notebook.filesOk_one: Reads {{count}} file with "Always allow" for this notebook.
notebook.filesOk_other: Reads {{count}} files with "Always allow" for this notebook.
notebook.filesPending: These files don't have "Always allow" for this notebook on this machine. The task doesn't ask or read them: the step will fail until you open the notebook, run the cell and choose "Always allow".
notebook.writeHint: A task runs a cell that writes to a table only if you authorize it here. If the table or the mode changes, it has to be authorized again.
notebook.paramsHint: Values for the notebook parameters on each run. They accept variables ({date}…).
notebook.saveHint: A copy with the results of this run (within the preview limits in Settings › Notebooks). The original is not modified.
notebook.exportFolderHint: Empty: where the copy goes or, if it isn't saved, next to the notebook.
notebook.chartsHint: A task exports the tables: charts are included when exporting from the app.
notebook.outputsHint: In the following steps: {steps.N.file} is the export (or the copy), {steps.N.html} the HTML export (for an email body) and {steps.N.notebook} the copy.

howTo.teams: In the Teams channel: “Workflows” › “Post to a channel when a webhook request is received”, and copy the URL it gives you.
howTo.slack: In Slack, create an app with “Incoming Webhooks” turned on and add a webhook for the channel: the URL starts with https://hooks.slack.com/.
howTo.telegram: Create a bot with @BotFather and copy its token. The chat is the number of the group or channel (with the bot as a member), or the @name of a public channel.
howTo.ntfy: The topic URL on ntfy.sh or on your own server (public and with https), for example https://ntfy.sh/my-topic. The token is only needed if the topic is protected.

problems.badUrl: Not a valid URL (and it can't contain a user name or password).
problems.notHttps: The URL must start with https://.
problems.teamsHost: The Teams webhook URL must be from Microsoft (logic.azure.com, api.powerplatform.com or webhook.office.com).
problems.slackHost: The Slack webhook URL must be from hooks.slack.com.
problems.ntfyLocal: The ntfy server must be public: it can't be this computer or the local network.
problems.ntfyTopic: The URL must be the topic's, for example https://ntfy.sh/my-topic.
problems.badToken: The token doesn't have the expected form.
problems.badChat: The chat must be a number (-100…) or a @channel.

message.testText: DBine test message: if you see this, the step is set up correctly.
message.textHint: Accepts the task variables. {results} is what each previous step did (✓ ok, ✗ failed, – didn't run) and {alerts} their alerts. Messages longer than 3,500 characters are cut.
message.privacy: The webhook URL and the tokens are stored in this computer's keychain, never in the task or the history. The message goes out only over HTTPS to the chosen service.

sections.dbineHint: The tasks DBine runs on this computer
sections.serversHint: The jobs each database server runs on its own

server.noConnections: No connection uses an engine with server jobs (SQL Server Agent, DBMS_SCHEDULER, Snowflake tasks, Databricks jobs, pg_cron, MySQL events…).
server.failedCount_one: {{count}} job failed on its last run
server.failedCount_other: {{count}} jobs failed on their last run
server.systemHint: System jobs come with the database or the engine: a user did not create them.

confirm.stop: Stop the current run of the job “{{job}}” on {{connection}}?
confirm.enable: Enable the job “{{job}}” on {{connection}}? It runs again on its schedule.
confirm.disable: Disable the job “{{job}}” on {{connection}}? It stops running on its schedule.
confirm.clearHistory: Delete the run history of job «{{job}}» on {{connection}}? This cannot be undone.

done.runFrom: The server started running «{{job}}» from step «{{step}}».

server.readOnly: Read-only connection: you can view the job, but not run, stop or enable it.
server.noHistory: This engine doesn't keep its jobs' run history.
server.systemObjectsHint: System objects come with the engine: a user did not create them.

runFromDialog.title: Start at step
runFromDialog.message: Job «{{job}}» runs now on {{connection}}, starting from the step you choose.

designer.readOnlyHint: It cannot be saved: the connection is read-only, or the server does not let this user change this object.
designer.invalid: Some fields need review: they are marked in red.

errors.required: This field must be filled in.
errors.missing: «{{value}}» is not among the options: choose another.
errors.minRows_one: At least one row is required.

designer.minRowsHint_one: It cannot be removed: the list needs at least one row.
designer.minRowsHint_other: It cannot be removed: the list needs at least {{count}} rows.
designer.secretKeep: Unchanged: leave it empty to keep the current one
designer.secretMasked: The script shows the secret values you typed as ********: only Save writes the real ones. If you open it in a query, replace them before running it.
designer.secretMaskedSave: The script shows the secret values you typed as ********; when saving, the real ones are written.
designer.secretComment: Secret values appear as ********: replace them with the real ones before running this script.
designer.dirtyClose: There are unsaved changes in «{{name}}». Close the tab and discard them?
designer.dirtyReload: There are unsaved changes in «{{name}}». Discard them and read it again from the server?
designer.confirmSave: Save the changes to «{{name}}» ({{kind}}) on {{connection}}? This script runs:
designer.confirmDelete: Delete «{{name}}» ({{kind}}) from {{connection}}? This script runs and cannot be undone:
designer.confirmAction: «{{action}}» will run on «{{name}}» ({{kind}}) on {{connection}}, with this script:
designer.actionForm: Fill in the values for «{{action}}» on «{{name}}» ({{kind}}) on {{connection}}. You will see its script before it runs.
designer.noScript: The server returned no script: there are no changes to save.

log.empty: The server has no scheduler logs.
